entry.title: Panofsky Prize, MicroBooNE
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab News reports that Sam Zeller was awarded the W.K.H. Panofsky Prize. The citation is for co-leadership of the MicroBooNE experiment at Fermilab, which advanced next-generation liquid-argon time projection chamber technology for neutrino detection.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab News reports that crews from Fermilab, CERN and SURF have started building the first of two large cryostats, the insulated containers that will hold liquid argon for DUNE. A second report describes the start of construction of the detector in South Dakota, with the University of Texas at Arlington involved in the field cage and other components. Colorado State University, a founding member of DUNE, also marked the construction milestone.

entry.title: SBND cross section
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SBND, the Short-Baseline Near Detector at Fermilab, measured the total and single-differential inclusive electron-neutrino charged-current cross sections on argon. The sample is a mixture of 95.2% neutrino and 4.8% antineutrino events. The authors describe it as the highest-statistics inclusive measurement of this channel on argon to date and the first one using the Booster Neutrino Beam.

entry.title: KM3NeT/ARCA diffuse search
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. KM3NeT published a search for a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux, over the full sky and from the Galactic Ridge, using the first ARCA configurations with 6, 8, 19 and 21 detection units (640 days of livetime in total). The all-sky fit under a single power law gives a spectral index of 3.00 with uncertainties of +0.30 and -0.35 at 68% credible level. The collaboration announced the paper on 20 November.

entry.title: JUNO ultrapure water
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. JUNO is a 20 kton liquid-scintillator detector designed primarily to determine the neutrino mass ordering. Because the scintillator touches ultrapure water during filling, the water must contain less than 50 μBq/m3 of radium. A new paper describes a measurement system sensitive to radium in water down to 3.9 μBq/m3 and an optimised 100 t/h production process that combines selective ion-exchange resin with membrane separation.

entry.title: Reactor source near JUNO
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A phenomenology paper proposes placing a movable reactor antineutrino source within about 3 km of the JUNO detector. The authors argue that no planned experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on θ13, and that JUNO's large fiducial mass would give a statistically significant event count from a relatively small reactor over a few years. This is a proposal, not an approved programme.

entry.title: Geoneutrino decay limits
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new analysis uses geoneutrinos to test neutrino decay for the first time. The authors compute the geoneutrino signal at Borexino, KamLAND, SNO+ and JUNO for visible decay and compare it with the published data. They find no evidence of decay that holds across Earth models.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CERN Courier reports that Francis Halzen was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. IceCube also released its 2027 calendar, with photographs taken by its winterovers at the South Pole.

entry.title: CYGNO electron directionality
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The CYGNO collaboration studied how well its optical time-projection chamber reconstructs the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils, using the 50 L LIME prototype with a scientific CMOS readout. Directionality could help separate solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds. The algorithm finds the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light and takes the direction from the early part of the ionisation trail, before multiple scattering erases it.

entry.title: MINERvA open dataset
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A paper presents a probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset. It maps generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables, without relying on generator-specific interaction labels. The aim is to let people outside the original collaboration compare interaction models with open neutrino data.

entry.title: The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which can occur alongs
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which can occur alongside the nucleonic Urca processes if Δ isobars are present in the dense core. The abstract says this contribution had not been explicitly determined before. It matters for neutron-star cooling, where Urca processes are the dominant neutrino-emitting mechanisms.

entry.title: The authors ask how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic-r
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors ask how well kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could determine the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, including uncertainties on neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. They also introduce a technique for reconstructing the primary spectrum.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase in open two-flavour neutrino oscillations. Every completely positive trace-preserving evolution that is covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to the phase. A rate anisotropy in the environment can supply a phase reference, and the paper gives the resulting finite-time dependence.

entry.title: This is a comparison of nine periodogram algorithms applied to the 22-year Super-Kamiokande solar 8B neutrino
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. This is a comparison of nine periodogram algorithms applied to the 22-year Super-Kamiokande solar 8B neutrino dataset (1996-2018). The authors find that the Generalized Lomb-Scargle method gives the most statistically robust detections because it handles heteroscedastic uncertainties correctly. The work is relevant to anyone searching for time modulation in solar neutrino rates.

entry.title: Hydrodynamic simulations of supernovae cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics, so they need subgrid schemes
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Hydrodynamic simulations of supernovae cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics, so they need subgrid schemes for the effect of neutrino self-interaction. The paper gives semianalytic approximations for the outcomes of slow and fast flavour conversion in quasihomogeneous systems. The authors report excellent agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering.

entry.title: The paper studies a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with the ph
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies a gauged U(1) Lμ-Lτ model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with the photon. This produces an effective matter potential in the Sun and modifies solar-neutrino oscillations through the MSW mechanism. The analysis uses recent Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande measurements and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD.
